name: OpenStack
tagline: Private IaaS: identity, KVM compute, virtual networks and block storage.
keyPoints: Keystone issues tokens; every service call is authenticated against it.
Nova schedules instances onto KVM hosts; Glance supplies the images.
Neutron builds L2 networks, L3 routers, security groups and floating IPs.
Cinder attaches persistent block volumes; Horizon is the web console.
quickDeploy: Harden SSH and set a static IP.
Create the stack user and clone DevStack.
osiNote: Neutron bridges L2 and routes L3; service APIs speak HTTP.
production: Run three controllers behind HAProxy and keepalived; cluster the database and RabbitMQ.
Back up the database and Glance images; test restores.
Put Cinder on replicated storage; snapshot before every change.
Rotate Keystone credentials; restrict API endpoints to management networks.
Alert on down agents, RabbitMQ queue depth and hypervisor free memory.

howItWorks.title: Identity (Keystone, L7)
howItWorks.body:
Users authenticate once and receive a scoped token.
The catalog lists every service endpoint by region.
Roles on a project decide what each token can do.
Every API checks the token before acting.

howItWorks.title: Compute and images (Nova, Glance)
howItWorks.body:
Nova API queues the request; the scheduler picks a KVM host.
nova-compute drives libvirt to boot the instance.
Glance serves the image the instance boots from.
Flavors fix vCPU, RAM and disk.

howItWorks.title: Networking (Neutron, L2/L3)
howItWorks.body:
Self-service networks are tenant overlays; provider networks map to a physical network.
OVN or OVS wires instance ports into bridges.
Routers give NAT; floating IPs map a public address in.
Security groups filter per port.

howItWorks.title: Block storage (Cinder)
howItWorks.body:
Cinder creates volumes on a backend such as LVM or Ceph.
A volume attaches to an instance as a virtual disk.
Snapshots and backups protect the data.
Volumes outlive the instance.

howItWorks.title: Control plane
howItWorks.body:
Services talk through REST APIs, a message queue and a database.
Horizon calls the same APIs as the openstack CLI.
Compute hosts run agents; controllers run the APIs.
HA means a clustered queue and database.

howItWorks.title: Connecting to its neighbours
howItWorks.body:
In front: users call REST APIs through the CLI or Horizon; an HAProxy virtual IP fronts the APIs in HA setups.
Behind: KVM hosts with libvirt, Open vSwitch or OVN, and Ceph or LVM storage.
Cluster API provider OpenStack or Magnum builds Kubernetes clusters on Nova instances.
cloud-provider-openstack maps Service type LoadBalancer to Octavia and PersistentVolumes to Cinder.
Keystone federates with an OIDC or SAML provider such as Keycloak.

howItWorks.title: Deployment tools
howItWorks.body:
DevStack is for labs; it installs everything on one machine from git.
kolla-ansible deploys containerised services; OpenStack-Ansible deploys into LXC containers.
Terraform, Heat or the openstack.cloud Ansible collection create projects and resources as code.

howItWorks.title: Operations
howItWorks.body:
Use the CLI for day-two tasks: openstack compute service list and network agent list.
A Prometheus OpenStack exporter and central logs watch the control plane and compute hosts.
Back up the database and Glance images; test the restore.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
Smaller scale: Proxmox or plain KVM with libvirt.
Vendor stacks: VMware vSphere with vCenter, or Microsoft Hyper-V.
Kubernetes-native virtualisation: KubeVirt on an existing cluster.
Public cloud: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud when owning hardware is not the goal.

flow: The client requests a token from Keystone.
Nova API validates the token and queues the boot request.
The scheduler selects a compute host with free resources.
Nova fetches the image from Glance.
Neutron creates the port and security group rules on the host bridge.
Cinder attaches the volume if requested.
libvirt starts the KVM guest; a floating IP exposes it.

deploy.summary: Single-node lab on Ubuntu 24.04 with DevStack. Harden the host first, then stack.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 VM or bare metal, 8 GB RAM minimum, 60 GB disk
A workstation with an SSH key pair
A second NIC if you want a real provider network

steps.title: 1. SSH key login and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ubuntu@192.168.1.50
sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-hardening.conf <<'CF'
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
MaxAuthTries 3
CF
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: Run ssh-copy-id from your workstation. Keep a second session open until a key login succeeds.

steps.title: 2. Static address with netplan
steps.code:
sudo tee /etc/netplan/01-static.yaml <<'CF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    enp1s0:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses: [192.168.1.50/24]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 192.168.1.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [192.168.1.1]
CF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/01-static.yaml
sudo netplan try
steps.note: netplan try rolls back after 120 seconds unless you confirm. Remove any conflicting cloud-init network file.

steps.title: 3. Hostname and firewall
steps.code:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname os01
echo '192.168.1.50 os01' | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 80 proto tcp
sudo ufw --force enable
steps.note: Allow only your admin subnet. Port 80 serves Horizon.

steps.title: 4. Create the stack user
steps.code:
sudo useradd -s /bin/bash -d /opt/stack -m stack
sudo chmod +x /opt/stack
echo 'stack ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/stack
sudo -u stack -i
steps.note: From the DevStack guide. The chmod avoids a permissions failure on Ubuntu 21.04 and later.

steps.title: 5. Clone DevStack and write local.conf
steps.code:
git clone https://opendev.org/openstack/devstack
cd devstack
cat > local.conf <<'CF'
[[local|localrc]]
ADMIN_PASSWORD=ChangeMe123
DATABASE_PASSWORD=$ADMIN_PASSWORD
RABBIT_PASSWORD=$ADMIN_PASSWORD
SERVICE_PASSWORD=$ADMIN_PASSWORD
HOST_IP=192.168.1.50
CF
steps.note: Use alphanumeric passwords only. Add PUBLIC_INTERFACE=<second NIC> to bridge guests to a physical network.

steps.title: 6. Run the installer
steps.code:
./stack.sh
source openrc admin admin
openstack service list
steps.note: Takes 15 to 30 minutes. It prints the Horizon URL and credentials at the end.

steps.title: 7. Image, keypair and security group rules
steps.code:
curl -LO https://download.cirros-cloud.net/0.6.2/cirros-0.6.2-x86_64-disk.img
openstack image create cirros-lab --file cirros-0.6.2-x86_64-disk.img --disk-format qcow2 --container-format bare --public
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/lab -N ''
openstack keypair create --public-key ~/.ssh/lab.pub lab
openstack security group rule create --proto icmp default
openstack security group rule create --proto tcp --dst-port 22 default
steps.note: DevStack already ships a CirrOS image; this shows the Glance upload. The private and public networks exist by default.

steps.title: 8. Boot, attach a volume, add a floating IP
steps.code:
openstack server create --flavor m1.tiny --image cirros-lab --network private --key-name lab test-server
openstack volume create --size 1 data01
openstack server add volume test-server data01
FIP=$(openstack floating ip create public -f value -c floating_ip_address)
openstack server add floating ip test-server $FIP
echo $FIP
steps.note: Wait for ACTIVE first: openstack server show test-server -c status.

verify: openstack token issue returns a token for the admin project.
openstack compute service list shows nova-compute up.
openstack network agent list shows all agents alive.
openstack server list shows test-server ACTIVE with a floating IP.
openstack volume list shows data01 in-use.
pitfalls: Passwords with special characters break DevStack services; use alphanumeric only.
Running stack.sh as root instead of the stack user fails early.
Without nested virtualization the guests fall back to slow QEMU emulation.
A reboot stops DevStack services; run stack.sh again for a lab rebuild.
Missing security group rules for ICMP and 22 look like a networking fault.
Provider networks need a NIC with no host IP; never reuse your SSH interface.
DevStack is for labs only; production uses kolla-ansible or OpenStack-Ansible.
